# Widget live re-runs

`pnpm widget:live` re-runs production widget investigations locally against the customer's own workspace, read-only, and scores the replies. Nothing is deployed and nothing is filed.

`pnpm widget:live <wrun id...> [--server <url>]` re-runs production investigations against the customer's own workspace (ENG-15026). Start a local `eve dev` with `WIDGET_LIVE=1`, no `VERCEL_ENV`, `.env.local` for Executor and `FOREMAN_DIAGNOSTICS_SECRET`. Live mode refuses every Vercel environment, including Preview. The runner requires `.env.prod-reader` for read-only production run lookup and Vercel CLI auth for stream decryption. Set `WIDGET_LIVE` only on the server, not the runner. The server must be an HTTP loopback origin (default `http://localhost:2000`); the runner checks its authenticated, data-free live-mode endpoint before sending a recorded scope or customer message, and refuses redirects.

The runner reads streams through `scripts/widget-run-stream.ts`. It compares each recorded read's exact input against its new output, ignoring only `observedAt`, key order and null fields. Failed or unavailable recordings and re-reads, including partial source failures, are excluded and listed as unverifiable. Actual comparable changes mean `state moved`; complete, nonempty unchanged evidence means `steady`; empty or incomplete unchanged evidence means `unverifiable`. Only steady evidence permits a future cause grade. Capability stays blank until ENG-15024's classifier replaces the named `gapSentences` seam; the report prints the original reply's limitation sentences beside the new reply.

The staff path keeps the result team-only. The local harness stamps the recorded original date, replaces every run-store dependency with filesystem persistence under `.eve/widget-live/runs/`, and `widget_file_ticket` returns a simulated ticket instead of filing. No external database writes or Linear ticket writes occur, regardless of the server's database URL. Local store transactions use a filesystem lock with a five-second acquisition deadline and atomic replacement; after a process dies while holding the lock, stop the server before removing `.eve/widget-live/runs/lock` to recover. All raw evidence and results remain under the gitignored `.eve/widget-live/`; printed text passes through the existing scrubber and leak check, and is withheld if identifiers remain.

Date enforcement lives at the tool boundary, not just in a prompt. For an omitted billing `creditWindow`, the ledger reads the original UTC conversation day, from midnight inclusive to the next midnight exclusive. For an owned campaign's omitted `startDate`/`endDate`, outreach metrics read seven calendar days ending on that original day, both ends inclusive. Explicit windows are preserved. Campaign listing has no historical date filter, and billing's current/lifetime balances and Stripe lists remain current even when its ledger is pinned. The exact-input drift re-read preserves the recorded input, including implicit moving windows; the report marks those calls so current default-window comparisons are not mistaken for pinned historical evidence. `widget_job_failures` and `widget_generation_diagnostics` (`since`), `widget_lead_pipeline_status` (`sinceDays`) and `widget_sdr_thread_status` (30 days) only take windows ending now; other authored tools take no absolute date input.

### Live scorecard

`pnpm widget:live score [--set <name>] [--pick 20] [--runs 1] [--server <url>]` turns live re-runs into the scorecard (ENG-15044 round 7), against the same local `eve dev` with `WIDGET_LIVE=1`. Nothing is deployed and every read stays read-only on the staff path.

The first time a set name is used (default: today's UTC date), the runner reads production `widget_support_runs` from the last 7 days through `.env.prod-reader`: completed investigations (`wrun_` sessions) from the customer widget, never team inbox runs, with the test and internal workspaces in `parseExcludedOrgs` (`agent/lib/widget-candidates.ts`, plus `WIDGET_CANDIDATES_EXCLUDE_ORGS`) excluded. Each conversation gives one run, its newest that admitted something it could not check or asked a clarifying question, else its newest. Runs are taken round-robin across billing, website, inboxes, campaigns, leads and other (keywords in the customer's message, first match in that order), admitting or asking runs first within a topic (`rankSet` in `agent/lib/widget-live-score.ts`). Each picked run's session stream is decrypted while it still exists and its customer message, recorded date, verified scope (including `recordingId`), original reply and original tool calls are saved to `.eve/widget-live/sets/<name>/set.json`; a stream that cannot be read is skipped and the next ranked run is taken, until `--pick` are saved. Later runs with the same `--set` reuse the file and never touch production, so a set outlives its 7-day streams.

Every case is then re-run live one at a time and judged by the local `claude -p` judge while the next one runs. Results go to `.eve/widget-live/sets/<name>/<timestamp>/`: one raw JSON per run, `records/` and `review.md` from the judge, `scorecard.md`, and `conversations.json` for the review page (per case the customer's messages, the original and new replies, each verdict with the judge's one-line reason, and the original and new tool calls, all through the existing scrubber; text it cannot clear is withheld). The judge sees only scrubbed text.

Live cases have no hand-written expectations, so nothing is invented as ground truth. Goals that need none are judged against the run's own tool results and guide sections: nothing made up, no leaks, stayed in budget, no tool gaps (with the same gap, unused and out-of-scope classes) and reply time. The rest use expectation-free stand-ins:

- `conclusion supported by the evidence read` replaces found the real cause: it is the judge's generic cause claim (the conclusion the question and tool results warrant), not an authored cause, and the column is labeled so it is never read as an authored cause. It keeps the 90% target that goal had.
- Answered what was needed is one fixed claim (the reply answers what was asked, or asks one clarifying question the tool results justify), plus context and reask on a later turn. Per-cause-type rows are dropped: live cases have no cause type.
- Handed off only when needed compares the run's handoff with one extra judge verdict, `needs_human`, decided from the customer's messages and tool results only. A run that sent no message gets that verdict alone.

Each case's original production reply is judged the same way against its own snapshotted tool results, into `production/` beside the live records, and `scorecard.md` opens with both side by side: production (what the customer got) and live at HEAD, then each column's full scorecard. The original's handoff reads the snapshot's saved outcome reason; it has no reply time. `conversations.json` carries the original's verdicts as `originalVerdicts`.

One run of 20 cases is noisy: the same behavior moved by ten points or more between runs (ENG-15044 round 12). `--runs N` (default 1) re-runs the whole set N times, each into `<timestamp>/run-<n>/` as a complete score result, then writes `<timestamp>/scorecard.md` with each goal as the mean pass rate over runs and its min and max; hit or miss is judged on the mean, and the header gives the run count. `pnpm widget:live score --set <name> --combine <dir> <dir> ...` reports saved score or rejudge results of one set the same way, using their saved verdicts and the set's current cause labels; it runs, judges and calls nothing, and writes `combined-<timestamp>/scorecard.md`. A directory name is read from the set's directory when it is not a path.

A live run that fails or does not complete is listed as `run_failed` and left out; a judge failure leaves the case as missing coverage, which withholds hit or miss.

## The claims judge

Every judge call (`pnpm widget:live score` and `rejudge`) runs through headless Claude Code on the local machine: `claude -p --model opus` with no tools, settings or MCP servers, the input on stdin and the reply held to the judge's JSON schema, at most three at once with a four-minute deadline each. Anthropic credentials are stripped from its environment, so it uses the local Claude Code login and never the AI Gateway, whose key is for Foreman itself only (Aaron, 2026-10-09). Records name the judge `claude-code/opus`. An investigate judgement carries the whole support guide (`SUPPORT_GUIDE`) as `productGuide`, a source for product and UI facts but never for facts about the customer's workspace. A keyword-picked 30,000-character slice left out sections that plainly worded answers relied on (round 9), and the whole guide judged no slower. The four-minute deadline starts once a judge slot is free, so time spent queued behind other calls does not count against it.

The claims judge also sorts every reply sentence saying something could not be confirmed, checked or was not available into `tool_gap` (data about the customer’s own Acquisity workspace that no widget tool reads, with a short name for the missing capability), `unused_capability` (a tool covers it but the investigator did not call it or lacked an input it could have asked for), `tool_failure` (a read errored or came back empty) `real_unknown` (the data does not exist) or `out_of_scope` (data the widget investigator must not have: another workspace or organization, the customer’s external bank, card issuer or mailbox provider records, or Acquisity-internal operations), stored as `gaps` on the judge record. The judge receives descriptions and input schemas from the actual tool definitions. The admission is never suppressed; a tool gap is fixed by adding the capability. Unused capabilities are ranked separately as investigator misses. Out-of-scope refusals are listed separately and do not count against no tool gaps.
